post.summary: Log in a human with email and password
post.description: Humans only. On success the response sets an HttpOnly session cookie (7 days, sliding) and returns 204. Wrong email, wrong password, inactive account and agent accounts all yield the same 401, so the response never reveals whether an email exists. Agents do not log in; they send 'Authorization: Bearer <api key>'.
Deletes the session cookie. Always 204, also without a session.

get.description: Returns the calling actor (human via session cookie, agent via API key) with its kind and instance scopes. For API-key calls, 'apiKey' holds the key's metadata: prefix, scope and workspace restrictions, expiry. 'mustChangePassword' is true when a human still uses the bootstrap password or one an admin set; they should choose their own with PATCH /api/v1/me/password (always false for agents). Agents should call this first to check which identity and rights a key carries.

patch.description: Humans with a session cookie only: sets 'newPassword' (12 to 256 characters) after checking 'currentPassword'. Returns 204 with a fresh session cookie; every other session of the account is signed out. Clears 'mustChangePassword'. A wrong 'currentPassword' yields 400 with code 'invalid_credentials' on that field, the same password again 400 'unchanged'. Agents and API-key calls get 403: they have no password.

get.description: The structures a new workspace can start with, for 'templateId' of POST /workspaces: 'id', 'name', 'description' and 'isDefault' (the template applied when 'templateId' is omitted). Any authenticated caller.
All humans and agents of the installation, ordered by name, including inactive ones. Requires instance:admin.

post.description: Creates a human or agent. 'kind' is 'human' or 'agent'. Humans need 'email' and may get an initial 'password' (min. 12 characters) for local login; agents get no password and authenticate with API keys (POST /api/v1/actors/{id}/keys). 'instanceScopes' is a subset of 'instance:admin', 'workspaces:create'. Requires instance:admin. A taken email yields 409 with code 'email_taken'.

get.description: One actor by id. Requires instance:admin.

patch.description: Partial update: omitted or null fields stay unchanged; role "" clears the role; 'instanceScopes' replaces the set. 'isActive': false deactivates the actor: no login, all its API keys are rejected. You cannot deactivate yourself or remove instance:admin from yourself (409 'self_lockout'). Requires instance:admin.

put.description: Sets 'newPassword' (12 to 256 characters) for a human, e.g. when they forgot it; creates the local login if the human has none yet. All existing sessions of that human are signed out (your own too, if you reset yourself; use PATCH /api/v1/me/password for that). 'mustChange' (default true) makes GET /api/v1/me report 'mustChangePassword' so the human picks their own password after logging in. Agents have no password: 400 with code 'not_human' on 'actorId'. Requires instance:admin.

post.summary: Issue an API key for an agent
post.description: Creates a key 'agck_<prefix>_<secret>' for an agent actor. The plain-text 'key' appears only in this 201 response; store it immediately, it cannot be retrieved again (only a hash is kept). Optional body: 'scopes' (subset of read, write, schema, admin; empty = the agent's membership rights apply in full), 'workspaceId' (restrict the key to one workspace), 'expiresAt' (future timestamp). Humans cannot get keys. Requires instance:admin.

get.description: Metadata of all keys of the actor, newest first, including revoked and expired ones. Never contains secrets. Requires instance:admin.

delete.description: Revokes the key immediately; further requests with it get 401. The key stays listed with 'revokedAt' for audit. Idempotent. Requires instance:admin.

get.description: Workspaces the caller is a member of, ordered by name, each with the caller's 'role' (owner, admin, editor, viewer) and effective 'scopes' (read, write, schema, admin; narrowed by the API key, if it is restricted). Archived workspaces are included with 'archivedAt'. A key restricted to one workspace sees only that one. Use 'slug' in /api/v1/w/{slug}/….

post.description: Creates a workspace; the caller becomes its owner. 'slug' (unique, immutable; lowercase letters, digits, single hyphens, max. 63) becomes the URL segment /api/v1/w/{slug}. 'name' is required, 'description' optional. 'templateId' chooses the starting structure: 'software-projekt' (default when omitted: spaces Produkt, Technik, Notizen with the collections Aufgaben, Analysen, Entscheidungen, Komponenten) or 'empty'; an unknown id yields 400 with the 'allowed' values (see GET /workspace-templates). The template is applied in the same transaction: if it fails, no workspace is created. Requires workspaces:create (instance:admin implies it). A taken slug yields 409 'slug_taken'.

get.description: The workspace with the caller's role and effective scopes. Requires read. Unknown slug or no membership: 404.

patch.summary: Change the schema of a collection
patch.description: Applies 'add' (new property definitions, appended), 'update' (by 'key'; only the given fields change; 'options' replaces the list; 'clearDefault' removes the default) and 'remove' (keys) together, or nothing. Prefer additive changes. Keys are immutable (400 'key_immutable': add a new property instead); types change only text ↔ markdown and select → multi_select (400 'type_change_not_allowed' with 'allowed'). Changes that lose stored values need 'confirmRemoval': true, otherwise 400 'removal_not_confirmed' naming what would be lost: removing properties, removing option values, lowering 'precision', markdown → text. Template presets are adjusted. Increments 'schemaVersion' (entries without an actual change do not); send 'expectedSchemaVersion' to get 409 'schema_version_conflict' instead of overwriting a concurrent change. Requires schema.

get.description: Views of the collection by sortOrder, then name. Every collection has the system views 'Tabelle' (table, default) and 'Rohdaten' (raw). A view says how records are presented: type, filter, sorts, groupBy and visibleProperties. 'needsAttention': true marks a board whose groupBy property was removed from the schema. Requires read.

post.description: Creates a view. Required: 'name' (unique in the collection, max. 100 characters) and 'type' (table, board, gallery, list, document, raw; timeline and calendar are not available yet). A board also needs 'groupBy': the key of a select or status property. 'filter' uses the filter DSL: { "and": [ … ] }, { "or": [ … ] } and { "not": { … } } around conditions { "prop", "op", "value" }; the operators depend on the property type and option values must exist (the rules of POST /collections/{id}/query, which lists the operator matrix; 'in'/'nin' take a list, 'is_empty'/'is_not_empty' no value). Run a view with POST /views/{id}/query. 'sorts': [ { "prop", "dir": "asc"|"desc" } ]. 'visibleProperties': property keys shown (empty = all). 'cardCoverProperty': gallery cover. All property keys must exist in the collection schema. 'isDefault': true makes it the default view. Invalid input: 400 with 'errors[]' and 'allowed' values. Requires write.

Unknown collection or space: 404.

post.description: Creates a record in a collection ('collectionId') or a free page in a space ('spaceId'). 'title' is required (max. 500 characters). 'properties' holds values by key as described by GET /collections/{id}/describe (JSON Schema); omitted properties get their default; relation values must be ids of records of the target collection, actor values ids of members. 'body' is Markdown (max. 2 MiB). The collection's default template (or 'templateId') provides preset values and the body when none is sent; sent values win. 'parentRecordId' nests the record below another one. Send an 'Idempotency-Key' header (e.g. a UUID) to make retries safe: the same key by the same actor within 24 h returns the first record instead of creating another. The response has no body; read it with GET ?includeBody=true. Requires write. Invalid values: 400 with 'errors[]' on 'properties.<key>' (e.g. 'unknown_property' or 'not_in_options' with 'allowed'); archived collection or space: 409.

Requires read.

patch.description: Partial update. 'properties' is a patch: only sent keys change, null removes a value (not for required properties). 'title' and 'body' replace the old values when sent; to add text without sending the whole body use POST …/append. Send 'expectedRevision' (the 'revision' you read) so concurrent changes are not overwritten: if the record moved on, 409 'revision_mismatch' carries 'currentRevision' and 'changedKeys' (title, property keys, body) changed since then; if your change does not touch them, retry with the current revision. Without 'expectedRevision' the last writer wins. 'reason' is stored with the revision. A change that changes nothing creates no revision. Requires write. Archived record: 409 'record_archived'.

Without 'section' it goes to the end of the body. Concurrent appends never overwrite each other. Creates a revision 'appended'. The body may not exceed 2 MiB: 400 'too_long' on 'markdown'. post.summary: Query the records of a collection
post.description: Filters, sorts and pages the records of a collection. Body (all optional): 'filter', 'sorts' [ { "prop", "dir": "asc"|"desc" } ] (max. 10; numbers numerically, dates chronologically, text alphabetically; empty values last; ties by creation time; multi_select, relation and json cannot be sorted), 'fields' (property keys to return; add "body" for the Markdown body), 'limit', 'cursor', 'includeArchived', 'includeCount'. Filter DSL: a node is { "and": [ … ] }, { "or": [ … ] }, { "not": { … } } or a condition { "prop", "op", "value" }; nest freely (max. 8 levels, 100 conditions). 'prop' is a property key of the collection or a pseudo-field (title, created_at, updated_at, created_by, updated_by; a schema property with the same key wins). Operators per type: text, markdown, url, email, title: eq, neq, contains, starts_with, in, nin, is_empty, is_not_empty; number: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, in, nin, is_empty, is_not_empty; checkbox: eq, neq, is_empty; select, status: eq, neq, in, nin, is_empty, is_not_empty; multi_select: contains, in, nin, is_empty, is_not_empty; date: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, is_empty, is_not_empty; datetime, created_at, updated_at: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, is_empty, is_not_empty; relation: contains, in, nin, is_empty, is_not_empty; actor, created_by, updated_by: eq, neq, in, nin, is_empty, is_not_empty; json: not filterable. 'in'/'nin' take a list (max. 100), 'is_empty'/'is_not_empty' no value (empty = missing, null, "" or []). 'contains'/'starts_with' on text are case-insensitive; 'contains' on multi_select/relation tests one value; 'in' on them means any of the values; 'neq'/'nin' also match records without a value. Values: numbers as JSON numbers, dates 'YYYY-MM-DD', date-times ISO 8601 with offset (or a date = start of day UTC), relation values record ids, actor values ids or 'actor:<id>', option values must exist in the schema. Example: { "and": [ { "prop": "status", "op": "in", "value": ["todo", "in_progress"] }, { "or": [ { "prop": "due", "op": "lt", "value": "2026-12-01" }, { "prop": "priority", "op": "eq", "value": "high" } ] } ] }. Results: 'items' (records without body unless requested), 'nextCursor' (pass as 'cursor' for the next page; null when there are no further matches) and, with 'includeCount': true, 'count' (all matches, at most 10000). 'limit' 1..500, default 50. Archived records only with 'includeArchived': true. Invalid input: 400 with 'errors[]' on the path (e.g. 'filter.and[1].op'), codes unknown_property, unknown_operator, operator_not_applicable, invalid_value, not_in_options, not_sortable, invalid_cursor, each with 'allowed' where there is a closed set; unknown body members (e.g. 'sort' instead of 'sorts') are 'unknown_property' with the accepted members as 'allowed'. Requires read.

'contains'/'starts_with' on text are case-insensitive; 'contains' on multi_select/relation tests one value; 'in' on them means any of the values; 'neq'/'nin' also match records without a value. Results: 'items' (records without body unless requested), 'nextCursor' (pass as 'cursor' for the next page; null when there are no further matches) and, with 'includeCount': true, 'count' (all matches, at most 10000). 'limit' 1..500, default 50. Archived records only with 'includeArchived': true. Invalid input: 400 with 'errors[]' on the path (e.g. 'filter.and[1].op'), codes unknown_property, unknown_operator, operator_not_applicable, invalid_value, not_in_options, not_sortable, invalid_cursor, each with 'allowed' where there is a closed set; unknown body members (e.g. 'sort' instead of 'sorts') are 'unknown_property' with the accepted members as 'allowed'. Requires read.

get.description: Activity events: who changed which record, space, collection or member, with a diff ('old'/'new' per changed field; for record bodies 'bodyChanged' and 'bodyDelta' {added, removed} characters). 'targetTitle' is the current title of the record, or name of the space or collection, null if the target no longer exists (and for members and views). Filters: spaceId, collectionId, actorId, targetId (the history of one record, space or collection), since (ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-11-06T00:00:00Z), types (repeatable: record.created, record.updated, record.appended, record.archived, record.restored, space.created, space.updated, space.archived, collection.created, collection.updated, collection.schema_changed, collection.archived, view.created, view.updated, view.deleted, member.added, member.updated, member.removed). Two modes. Without afterSeq: newest first, paginated with 'limit' (1..200) and 'cursor' (nextCursor of the previous page); for a look back ('what happened since yesterday?'). With afterSeq: forward, in commit-safe order (transaction order), only events that are final; for keeping up with changes. Start with afterSeq=0 (whole log) or with 'lastSeq' of a newest-first response (from now on), then call again with the 'lastSeq' of each response; with a full page call again at once, otherwise poll. Only lastSeq is a safe cursor: never pass the seq of an item, it can skip events. This never skips an event, even when transactions commit in another order than their seq: a lower seq can follow a higher one, and lastSeq is the seq of the last event, not always the highest. Do not poll with 'since': 'at' is taken before the commit, so an event can appear later with an 'at' before your last poll. afterSeq and cursor do not combine. Requires read.

parameters.name: afterSeq
parameters.description: Read forward after this position: 0 for the whole log, otherwise 'lastSeq' of the previous response.

get.summary: Full-text search over all records of the workspace
get.description: Finds records by words in title, properties and body across all spaces and collections, without knowing the collection or the filter DSL (for exact property conditions use POST /collections/{id}/query). Input: 'q'. Syntax (web search style, case-insensitive, no stemming): words separated by spaces must all occur; "exact phrase" in double quotes; -word excludes; 'or' between alternatives (e.g. postgres or mongodb). The last word, if it has at least 2 letters or digits, also matches as a prefix (entsch finds Entscheidung) unless it is quoted or excluded; in a hyphenated word only the last part is a prefix (foo-ba does not find foo-bar). At least one word must not be excluded. 1..200 characters. Searched: title (ranks highest), text, markdown, url and email properties (the first 25000 characters together), the labels and values of select, status and multi_select options, and the first 75000 characters of the body (the rest of a long body is not indexed). E-mail addresses and hosts are single words (kontakt finds kontakt@firma.example, firma does not). Not searched: relations, actors, numbers, dates, json, comments. Records in an archived collection or space count as archived. Each hit has 'snippet': plain text with every match between ⟦ and ⟧ (U+27E6, U+27E7). The snippet can contain <, > and markup from the content: render it as text, never as HTML. Only these two markers come from the server (in content they appear as [ and ]). Without markers when only the title matched or the match lies beyond the first 20000 characters. 'rank': higher is better, 1 or more when the title matches the whole query. Ordered by rank, then id. Filters: spaceId, collectionId (unknown: 404), includeArchived (default false; also records of archived collections and spaces). 'limit' 1..50, default 20; 'nextCursor' with the same 'q' gives the next page, null when there are no further hits. Invalid input: 400 with errors[] on 'q' (required, empty_query when nothing is left to search for, too_long, invalid_value for control characters), 'limit' (out_of_range) or 'cursor' (invalid_cursor). Requires read.
